title: The Raise Math Nobody Teaches You

beats.say: A bonus can make your paycheck feel surprisingly small, but it's not because you moved into a higher tax bracket.
beats.visual: Cinematic shot of a single pen resting on a blank desk, moody low-key studio lighting, shallow depth of field.

beats.say: People think crossing into a higher tax bracket means losing money on your entire salary.
beats.visual: Close up of an abstract tax document viewed from a steep angle, blurred out text, cool blue cinematic tones.

beats.say: That is completely false. Marginal brackets only apply to the dollars sitting above that specific income line.
beats.visual: Close up of hands shuffling through blank index cards on a dark wooden surface, warm side lighting.

beats.say: Marginal tax brackets mean you always take home more when you earn more, but supplemental withholding on bonuses can temporarily take a bigger bite upfront.
beats.visual: A sleek modern desk lamp casting a sharp shadow over a blank ledger notebook, cinematic shadows.

beats.say: When your employer pays a bonus, federal rules often mandate a flat twenty-two percent withholding rate.
beats.visual: Close up of a calculator screen showing blurred numbers, backlit by soft ambient room light.

beats.say: If that flat rate sits higher than your normal tax bracket, your net payout looks noticeably lighter than expected.
beats.visual: An open calendar book on a dark table, soft morning light filtering through window blinds, quiet mood.

beats.say: You don't lose that money permanently—any over-withholding comes back as a tax refund when you file.
beats.visual: Close up of a metal paperclip resting on a clean white sheet of paper, moody overhead lighting.

beats.say: Understanding this cash flow dip stops you from panicking when your annual bonus hits your account.
beats.visual: A dark ceramic coffee cup sitting on a minimalist wooden coaster, steam rising slowly in soft window light.

beats.say: Always check your yearly tax return to ensure your total withholding matches your actual liability.
beats.visual: An overhead shot of a closed leather notebook resting on a stark concrete tabletop, dramatic shadows.

beats.say: Mastering the mechanics of your paycheck keeps you in control of your financial growth.
beats.visual: A sleek mechanical pencil lying diagonally across a blank sheet of paper, dark moody aesthetic.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A minimalist dark hallway with a single beam of warm light hitting the polished floor, cinematic framing.

caption:
Ever wonder why your bonus check has way more taxes taken out than your normal salary? It's all about withholding rules, not tax brackets. 

#paycheck #taxes #personalfinance #moneymindset #financiallit
description: Learn the exact mechanics behind payroll tax withholding on bonuses and raises. Understand why net pay drops temporarily and how tax refunds fix the gap.
first_comment: Did your last bonus surprise you with how much was withheld?
